counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span showing a low plasma zinc level; 72 μg/dL is within the reference range
No raw span linking elevated TSH to the skin biopsy or plaque morphology
No raw span for periorificial dermatitis, alopecia, or diarrhea that would support zinc deficiency
decisive_items: well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, focal subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis
response.rationale: R3 alone integrates the psoriasiform plaque morphology, extensor distribution, and biopsy findings of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and lymphocytic infiltrate. R4 is a distant runner-up because the biopsy pattern can be seen in zinc deficiency, but its only raw zinc span is within normal range. R2 is rejected because elevated TSH is not connected to the skin biopsy and does not explain parakeratosis, subcorneal clefting, or keratinocyte necrosis.

rejected.why: Elevated TSH supports hypothyroidism, but no raw span links it to the psoriasiform plaques or the biopsy; hypothyroidism does not explain parakeratosis, subcorneal clefting, or keratinocyte necrosis.
